Parable

PAIR-uh-bul -- Greek parabole, 'a placing beside': a story laid beside real life to reveal a moral. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Parable is a short story that illustrates a moral lesson.

The teacher ended the assembly with a parable about a farmer whose patience saved his whole village.

Worked Example

Instead of lecturing her grandchildren about greed, a grandmother tells them a brief tale of a dog who drops his bone into a river while snapping at his own reflection.

A short story told to teach a moral lesson is exactly what a parable is. Unlike 'anecdote,' which simply recounts an amusing incident, a parable exists to make its listeners wiser.

How Parable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

fable

fable: a short tale, often with animals, that teaches a lesson

allegory

allegory: a story whose characters stand for deeper meanings

tale

tale: a short narrative or story

Antonyms

chronicle

chronicle: a factual record of events in order

report

report: a factual account of something observed

How Strong Is It? — fable → parable → allegory

fable vs. parable

fable vs. parable: Fable and parable are close cousins -- a fable usually stars talking animals and ends in a stated moral, while a parable tends to use ordinary human situations to carry its lesson.

allegory vs. parable

allegory vs. parable: Allegory is bigger and more elaborate than parable: a parable is a brief story with one clear moral, while an allegory can run the length of a whole book, with every character standing for something.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — para-

Prefix — para-: beside, alongside (Greek)

Root — ble

Root — ble: a throwing (from Greek ballein, 'to throw'; Greek parabole meant 'a throwing beside')

Put it together

Put it together: Para- ('beside, alongside') + ble ('a throwing' — from Greek ballein, 'to throw'; Greek parabole meant 'a throwing beside'): a parable is a comparison laid alongside real life — the same Greek root that gives us parabola and hyperbole.

Use the root in a new word: parabola

Use the root in a new word: parabola: The basketball traced a perfect parabola as it arced toward the hoop.
